name: Pushable Block
description: The grid-snapped crate: a body the player relocates one tile at a time. It owns the push rules — the pusher must be grounded, aligned to a face, and pushing into a free tile — and it owns the settle, because 'the block has arrived' is a fact other components build on (pressure plates weigh it, pits swallow it). Snapping to the grid is deliberate: free-physics crates drift off plates and wedge in doorways, and the puzzle stops being about intent. This component does not own what the block is for — world.pressure_plate decides whether a resting block matters. It does not own falling either; gravity stays with movement.physics_core, which is why canFall is a flag here and not a physics reimplementation. Climbability is likewise not its business: movement.ledge_grab decides what is grabbable.

inputs.name: gridSize
inputs.description: The tile size pushes snap to. Must match the level's collision grid or pushes will fight the geometry.

inputs.name: pushSpeed
inputs.description: Tile-crossing speed during a push. Slow enough to read as effort, fast enough that repositioning a crate never feels like a tax.

inputs.name: requiresGroundedPusher
inputs.description: Whether mid-air pushes are rejected. Almost always true — airborne shoves let players solve crate puzzles without ever landing, which unthreads the intended route.

inputs.name: canFall
inputs.description: Whether the block obeys gravity when pushed off a ledge. Falling crates enable drop-the-key puzzles; floating ones are for purely planar rooms.

inputs.name: pushCooldownSeconds
inputs.description: Dead time after a push settles before the next can start. Without it, a held input slides the block continuously and the grid snap becomes cosmetic.

outputs.name: isSettled
outputs.description: True only when the block is snapped to the grid and at rest — the state a pressure plate can trust.
